page: Amazon Web Services r9gd.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom AWS Graviton processor built on the arm64 64-bit architecture, delivering 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance provisions 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core, designed to support data-intensive and memory-constrained processing pipelines.

Storage and network I/O are handled with dedicated low-latency hardware. The instance includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume directly attached to the host, offering high-throughput, low-latency scratch space compared to networked block storage. Networking capability is set to a baseline speed of 1 Gbps. The instance does not include graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton arm64 architecture combined with a 1:8 memory configuration allows for efficient resource utilization in memory-heavy software environments. Because CPU allocation is dedicated without hardware multithreading overhead, each core delivers predictable single-threaded throughput. Workloads running on r9gd.large must be compiled or compatible with arm64 architectures, and local storage requires appropriate persistence strategies since instance store volumes are ephemeral.

Amazon Web Services r9gd.large is well suited for in-memory caching systems, distributed key-value stores, transactional databases requiring high RAM ratios, local temporary buffer storage, real-time analytics engines, and general memory-intensive arm64 workloads.
